question: Which of the following is the most electropositive element?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cs**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cs (Cesium)** is the** most electropositive element**.
 
• Electropositivity refers to the ability of an element to donate electrons and form positive ions (cations).
 
• Cesium is located in Group 1 of the periodic table, which consists of alkali metals known for their high electropositivity.
 
• Among the alkali metals, cesium has the lowest ionization energy, making it the most electropositive element.
 
• Other elements listed like **Mg (Magnesium), Ca (Calcium), and Na (Sodium)** are also electropositive but not as much as cesium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electropositivity** **decreases across a period from left to right** and **increases down a group** in the periodic table.
 
• Alkali metals are highly electropositive due to their single electron in the outermost shell, which they can easily lose to form a cation.
 
• Cesium's position at the bottom of Group 1 accounts for its high electropositivity.
 
• This property of cesium makes it highly reactive, especially with water, where it reacts explosively.
